_note: Accessibility for the DATA-extra (non-state-park) swim spots, keyed by slug. verified=true only where the operator's own page states the feature. Where a fact comes from a third-party guide it is named in `source` and verified stays false. Unknown fields are null rather than guessed.

hart-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: The swimming area is entered from a bulkhead and steps; it is one of the largest spring-fed swim areas in Florida and gets deep away from the edge. A half-mile boardwalk follows the spring run to the Suwannee River and is described as wheelchair-friendly. No published depth at the entry point and no chair lift.
hart-springs-park.service_animals_note: Pets are banned from the day-use springs area; the park does not publish a service-animal policy, so call (352) 463-3444 before relying on one.
hart-springs-park.source: Gilchrist County does not publish an accessibility page. Accessible parking, entrance, restrooms and the wheelchair-friendly boardwalk are reported by third-party guides (VisitFloridaSprings, Florida Birding Trail), not by the park.

lithia-springs-conservation-park.depth_at_entry_note: The fenced swim area has a shallow end where inflatable rings and toys are allowed and a roped deep end where no flotation devices are permitted. Hillsborough County does not publish depths or an accessible entry route into the spring.
lithia-springs-conservation-park.service_animals_note: Hillsborough County states that pets and service animals are not permitted inside the spring area (official). Service animals are otherwise allowed in the park.
lithia-springs-conservation-park.source: Hillsborough County publishes no accessibility detail for the spring beyond the service-animal restriction; the park map and brochure PDFs do not describe an accessible entry. Call (813) 744-5572.

hunter-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: A small sand beach slopes into a roped-off swim area on Kings Bay; the spring vent is about 100 feet offshore and the bottom drops away past the ropes. The city does not publish an accessible beach route or a beach wheelchair.
hunter-springs-park.service_animals_note: No dogs or pets in the park; service animals are permitted under Titles II and III of the ADA (official).
hunter-springs-park.source: City of Crystal River park page lists amenities and rules but no accessibility features. Call the park ranger on 352-697-0933.

little-river-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: Paved parking and paved sidewalks lead to two overlook decks above the spring; getting into the water is by the bank and steps, and the pool drops off steeply toward the cave mouth. No published depth at the entry point.
little-river-springs-park.service_animals_note: No pets allowed; the county does not publish a service-animal policy. Restrooms are portable units, so an accessible stall is not assured.
little-river-springs-park.source: Suwannee County Parks & Recreation states three handicap-accessible pavilion areas, paved parking and paved sidewalks; restrooms are portable.

royal-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: Two sets of stairs lead into the spring and there is a jumping platform above the boil, which is deep. The county publishes no accessible route to the water and no depths.
royal-springs-park.service_animals_note: No pets allowed; the county does not publish a service-animal policy. Restrooms are portable units.
royal-springs-park.source: Suwannee County Parks & Recreation lists stairs, a diving/jumping platform, a pavilion and portable restrooms, but no accessibility features.

suwannee-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: Entry is over the uneven limestone of an 1800s spring house and down the natural river bank to the sand bars. No steps, ramp, handrail or accessible route is published, and the walls are slick.
suwannee-springs-park.service_animals_note: Dogs are allowed on District lands on a leash; no specific service-animal policy is published.
suwannee-springs-park.source: Suwannee River Water Management District tract page lists a picnic area, restrooms and a canoe launch but publishes no accessibility detail. Call 386.362.1001.

otter-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: The county publishes nothing about how you get into the spring in the picnic area, or about the pool's entry. The pool is heated in winter and may be the more predictable option for someone who needs a rail or a ladder.
otter-springs-park.service_animals_note: No pet or service-animal policy is published for the day-use area.
otter-springs-park.source: Gilchrist County resumed management of the park in February 2026 and has not published accessibility information. Call (352) 463-0800.

morrison-springs-park.depth_at_entry_note: Wheelchair-accessible boardwalks and ramps run to the diver's dock and to the beach area, so you can get to the water's edge; the last step into the spring is over the sand beach. The pool itself is deep, with cavern openings and a cavity reaching about 300 feet.
morrison-springs-park.service_animals_note: Walton County publishes no pet or service-animal policy for the park.
morrison-springs-park.source: Walton County Amenities page states wheelchair-accessible boardwalks and ramps to the diver's dock and beach area, and handicapped parking near the pavilions.

vortex-spring.depth_at_entry_note: The basin is entered from decks, docks, platforms and a slide; the operator publishes no accessible entry route or depths, and everyone signs a waiver before swimming.
vortex-spring.service_animals_note: Qualifying service animals are permitted anywhere guests may go; other pets are limited to designated campground areas (official).
vortex-spring.source: Vortex Spring Adventures publishes rules and a pet/service-animal policy but no accessibility information. Call the dive shop on (850) 836-4979.

williford-spring.depth_at_entry_note: A boardwalk system rings the spring and runs out to Econfina Creek, and entry steps with handrails lead down into the spring. The boil is deeper than it looks; no depths are published. Toilets are composting units, so an accessible stall is not assured.
williford-spring.service_animals_note: The District publishes no service-animal policy for this site; dogs are generally allowed on District lands under control.
williford-spring.source: Northwest Florida Water Management District site page lists mobility access, the boardwalk system and entry steps with handrails into the spring.

pitt-spring-recreation-area.depth_at_entry_note: An extensive trail and boardwalk system links the springs, and the swimming area has safety railings; tube put-in and take-out docks sit at either end of the run. The District does not publish an accessible route into the water or any depths. Toilets are composting units.
pitt-spring-recreation-area.service_animals_note: The District publishes no service-animal policy for this site; dogs are generally allowed on District lands under control.
pitt-spring-recreation-area.source: Northwest Florida Water Management District site page lists boardwalks, docks and a railed swimming area; 'mobility' access is listed for the Econfina Creek area as a whole but not specifically for this site.

cypress-spring.depth_at_entry_note: There is no road access and no facilities: you arrive by kayak, canoe or boat on Holmes Creek and get in from the vessel or the natural bank. The District's 2026 restoration project is adding boardwalks and steps at the entry and exit points, but until that is finished there is no built entry at all.
cypress-spring.service_animals_note: No service-animal policy is published; there is no staffed entrance.
cypress-spring.source: Northwest Florida Water Management District describes Holmes Creek access as primarily by boat and has an open shoreline-restoration project at the spring; no accessibility information is published.
